subject: Prefetch regression — request for provisional rate carveout to cover launch delay
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@helixhealth.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency regression + launch delay — need commercial remediation

Aditya —

Quick summary: our integration with Redwood's prefetch/KV path regressed after the 06/30 runtime update. We observed 3x tail latency for 90+ token prompts over the weekend, which blocked our scheduled launch of HelixCare triage on Friday. The product team pushed the launch and procurement is asking for a commercial remediation while you prioritize a fix.

Attachments: helix_prefetch_logs_0708.txt (sample traces), timeline.csv (internal)

Ask: can Redwood provide a temporary rate carveout or one-time credit to cover the customer-facing launch impact while your engineering team stabilizes the runtime? We are sensitive to public commitments; ideally a 3-month accommodation or an invoice credit to make HelixHealth whole for the delayed launch window.

I can be available for a 20-minute sync this afternoon if helpful.

Thanks,
Sam Park
Director, Platform Integrations
HelixHealth
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@helixhealth.com>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency regression + launch delay — need commercial remediation

Team — looping you in. Helix reports a regression tied to our prefetch/KV changes; they pushed their launch and are requesting a commercial make-good while we prioritize a fix.

High-level asks for this thread:
- Sales: propose a commercial remedy we can commit to today (cap, term, conditionality).
- Product/Eng: confirm scope and realistic ETA for a fix and whether a targeted backport / hotfix is possible within 10 business days.
- Finance: provide guidance on the economic impact (run-rate, one-time credit vs discount) and whether you can approve a provisional accommodation before formal CCR/legal signoff.

Initial context from Helix: they want either a 3-month temporary rate reduction or a one-time invoice credit to offset the launch window. Their ARR footprint on Redwood is material for our Q3 motion; happy to share ARR details in the sync.

Marissa — can you draft a conservative commercial proposal we can present to Sam? Ben — is there wiggle room for a $Xk provisional credit to avoid immediate churn? Maya / Karthik — can you outline the engineering remediation plan and whether we can trade a smaller credit for a prioritized backport?

I propose a quick 11am slot if everyone is free — otherwise share your recs in thread.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks for pulling this together, Aditya. Sam — apologies for the disruption and thanks for the logs.

Commercial proposal (first pass):
- Option A (one-time): $40,000 invoice credit applied within next billing cycle.
- Option B (term): 3-month 40% rate reduction on generation tokens, capped at $45,000 total.
- Conditions: (1) Helix signs the attached amended SOW (DocuSign link) within 7 business days; (2) Redwood receives confirmation of the revised launch date and telemetry access for the next 30 days; (3) if fix is delivered within 10 business days, credit is reduced pro rata.

Attachments: commercial_proposal_v2.pdf (proposed language & DocuSign link)

Rationale: Option A simplifies billing and avoids multi-month reconciliation. Option B preserves short-term ARR while providing runway for their launch. I'm proposing conservative numbers to keep finance comfortable. Ben — can you provisionally approve Option A up to $40k while legal/CCR processes the paperwork?

If everyone agrees, I can send a framed email to Sam with the two options and the DocuSign link.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency regression + launch delay — need commercial remediation

Thanks for the ping — and apologies to Sam and the Helix team for the customer impact. Quick technical update:

- Root cause: an attention-cache invalidation regression introduced in the 06/30 runtime build that affects KV-prefetch for sequences >64 tokens under our new batching path.
- Scope: affects ~3% of production calls for accounts with mixed short/long prompt mixes (Helix is in that bucket).
- Fix plan: engineering has a prioritized hotfix branch; we can push a targeted backport to Helix's dedicated pool in ~7 business days if we perform a limited rollout and validation. Full rollout to hosted fleet will follow after QA.
- Mitigations: we can enable an interim prefetch fallback that reduces tail latency at the cost of modest throughput loss for a week.

Ask for trade: if Sales/Finance can frame a provisional accommodation (Option A or B), Product can commit to the targeted backport plus prioritized monitoring and a postmortem. If the backport is validated within 10 business days, we recommend pro-rating the commercial accommodation.

I've attached a draft postmortem and the proposed rollout timeline.

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Product Management (Serving)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md

Team — after reviewing the impact and the proposed options, Finance will provisionally approve Option A: a one-time invoice credit of $40,000 to be applied on the next invoice for HelixHealth. This approval is conditional on:

1) Legal/CCR receiving the signed SOW amendment via DocuSign within 7 business days (link in Marissa's proposal).
2) Engineering confirming the hotfix is scheduled for targeted rollout and sharing validation metrics within 10 business days.
3) If the hotfix is validated within that 10-business-day window, the credit will be reduced pro rata (our calculations are in the HubSpot deal notes).

Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Approved by: Ben Carter (provisional) — final posting contingent on CCR processing.
